John Legend And Pharrell Williams Join Forces For New Album ‘Muse’

Sep 9, 2026
Facebook
Twitter
Pinterest
WhatsApp
Linkedin
ReddIt
Email
Print
    Listen to audio version of this article
    Sponsored by
    0:00 / 4:07
    Instaread

    John Legend is stepping outside the formula that has defined much of his career with ‘Muse,’ a new 16-song album produced entirely and co-written by Pharrell Williams. Arriving October 23, the project is the first full album the longtime friends have created together and moves through gospel, doo-wop, classic soul, Afrobeat and hip-hop, with new single “Daylight” offering the first taste. Legend debuted the song with a performance from Nashville during CBS’s ‘America’s Tailgate’ special.

    The collaboration came together after Legend appeared on Clipse’s comeback album ‘Let God Sort ’Em Out,’ where his vocal on “The Birds Don’t Sing” caught Pharrell’s attention. The pair had known each other for more than two decades without making a full project together, and Pharrell saw an opportunity to build an album specifically around Legend’s voice.

    They began writing and recording in Paris in January 2025 at Pharrell’s studio inside Louis Vuitton headquarters. Rather than leaning into the piano ballads most closely associated with Legend, they pulled inspiration from Nina Simone, Nat King Cole and Marvin Gaye while combining orchestral textures with modern rhythms. Legend describes the concept as having a “Black James Bond aesthetic,” an idea that gives ‘Muse’ a cinematic framework without disconnecting it from the traditions of Black music that shaped both artists.

    The collaboration first surfaced publicly through “Pray For Ya,” a gospel-tinged track used during Louis Vuitton’s Fall-Winter 2026 Men’s show and later featured in Pharrell’s Moët Ice Impérial campaign. ‘Muse’ expands that sound into a much broader project, with Pharrell appearing across several tracks and Clipse joining Legend on “Bodies On The Floor.”

    The title track opens the record with a fictional relationship between a man and his muse, moving through attraction, commitment and betrayal against a backdrop of Paris and high art. The title also reaches further back to the nine Muses of Greek mythology, while Legend connects the concept to the musical predecessors whose work continues to shape his own songwriting.

    That relationship between history and experimentation runs throughout the album. “Her” draws from doo-wop and gospel, while “Get Back” pushes the record’s cinematic soul into horns and strings. “Are You OK?” turns a relationship argument into tough love, and “Bodies On The Floor” uses the vocabulary of violence to portray an intense and destructive relationship.

    ‘Muse’ also required Legend to give Pharrell an unusual amount of creative control. Legend recorded songs written entirely by Pharrell, something he says he almost never does, making trust an essential part of the process. That willingness to loosen his usual approach fits an album deliberately designed to challenge expectations surrounding what a John Legend record should sound like.

    More than 20 years into a career filled with signature ballads, Legend is using ‘Muse’ to resist the temptation to simply repeat what has already worked. The album may draw heavily from classic musical traditions, but the goal is not nostalgia. Legend and Pharrell are using those influences as raw material for something built around the particular combination of their voices, instincts and musical histories.

    Outside the album, Legend is also moving further into theatre. He is working on ‘Imitation of Life,’ a new musical opening at The Shed in November with a book by two-time Pulitzer Prize winner Lynn Nottage and direction by Whitney White. The production features Legend’s first original score for the stage.

    With ‘Muse,’ that appetite for new territory extends directly into his recording career. Pharrell’s production gives Legend a reason to move beyond the piano-led sound listeners know best, while the album’s mix of gospel, soul, hip-hop and cinematic orchestration keeps his musical history firmly within reach.

    ‘Muse’ Tracklist:

    1. “Muse” featuring Pharrell Williams
    2. “Pray For Ya”
    3. “Her Introduction”
    4. “Her” featuring Pharrell Williams
    5. “Daylight”
    6. “Get Back” featuring Pharrell Williams
    7. “Are You OK?” featuring Pharrell Williams
    8. “Under The Bridge Introduction”
    9. “Under The Bridge”
    10. “Next Time” featuring Pharrell Williams
    11. “Bodies On The Floor – Taps Introduction”
    12. “Bodies On The Floor” featuring Clipse
    13. “Doing Me”
    14. “Fireflies” featuring Pharrell Williams
    15. “Everything”
    16. “Sail Off”
